clue.text: Religious ascetic shivered, losing some energy going round

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so one letter is dropped from the word before
letters that go round are spun about and land in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy; one of the two Es goes

explanation.surface: A holy man in the desert trembles as his strength runs out while he wanders around.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one E is lost, which is why the clue says 'some' energy; the remaining seven letters are rearranged into the ascetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dervish is a member of a Sufi Muslim order who has taken vows of poverty and austerity, the whirling dervishes being famous.

clue.text: It’s raised in surprise by cockney sounding intellectual

indicators.note: a cockney speaker drops the initial H, and 'sounding' tells us to go by the pronunciation

blocks.note: a highbrow is an intellectual; said with the H dropped it becomes this facial feature

explanation.surface: Something an intellectual Londoner lifts when taken aback.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, famous for dropping the H at the start of words, so HIGHBROW is heard as 'eye-brow'.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift the arch of hair above each eye when astonished, so it is literally something raised in surprise.

clue.text: Struggles over wife making scenes

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it, so the outer word wraps round the smaller one

blocks.note: vies means competes or struggles
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man fights with his wife and the arguments become public rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making scenes' reads as causing a fuss, but scenes here are sights or vistas.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenes and views are synonyms for landscapes or prospects seen from a particular spot.

clue.text: Small bank with little in reserve?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a bank is an institution that lends money

explanation.surface: A tiny bank that keeps hardly any money in its reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition continues the banking picture; slender means meagre, as in slender means or a slender margin, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender resources are scanty or barely sufficient, which matches having little held back for emergencies.

clue.text: Decision by court on composer

indicators.note: in an across clue, placing one thing on another means it follows after it

blocks.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling about a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads naturally as a court deciding a composer's case, but court is just the abbreviation, tacked on after the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the formal finding of a jury or judge, so it is the decision reached at the end of a trial.

clue.text: Rebuke conservative abandoning safeguard

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to censure is to reprimand formally
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A politician is reprimanded for dropping a protective measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safeguard' looks like a noun completing the story, but it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To safeguard an outcome is to make certain of it or protect it, which is what ensuring does.

clue.text: US politicians protest about deserters

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
C stands for circa, Latin for about
rats are those who desert a sinking ship

explanation.surface: American politicians complain about turncoats in their party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a preposition linking protest to deserters, but it supplies C, the circa abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Democrats are one of the two major parties in American politics, opposite the Republicans.

clue.text: Setting in which to study manuscript

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a manuscript is a written text

explanation.surface: A library reading room where scholars examine old documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Con, meaning to study closely, survives mostly in crosswords and in 'conning' lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Context is the surrounding circumstances or background of an event, which is what its setting provides.

clue.text: Revolutionary chaplain a true star

indicators.note: revolution overturns the existing order, so the following letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radical army padre is hailed as a genuine celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' reads as a famous person praising the chaplain, but it is an astronomical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is the nearest star system to the Sun and the brightest point of light in the constellation Centaurus.

clue.text: Healthcare regime decentralised in this place

indicators.note: with the centre taken away only the edges remain, so just the end letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A health service run regionally rather than from the centre, in this very place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decentralised' sounds like a policy word about devolved health services, but it strips the middles from the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb indicating the speaker's present location is a direct synonym for at or in this spot.

clue.text: Voluntary action that makes one grunt in the US

definitions.text: Voluntary action that makes one grunt in the US

blocks.clueFragment: Voluntary action that makes one grunt
blocks.note: surface reading: some effort that makes a person groan with exertion
setter's reading: grunt is American slang for an infantry soldier, so this is signing up to the army

explanation.surface: Some strenuous activity you take on willingly that leaves you groaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Grunt looks like a verb for the noise of effort, but it is a noun: US slang for a low-ranking foot soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining the armed forces voluntarily, rather than by conscription, is what turns a civilian into a soldier.

clue.text: Epoch starts to see every dinosaur wiped out

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: an epoch is an era
the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: The start of a geological age witnesses the extinction of all the dinosaurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epoch starts' reads as the beginning of an age, but Epoch stands alone and 'starts' applies to the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out is to remove every trace of it, the sense of erased as obliterated.

clue.text: Counsel care, having captured returning hero

indicators.note: something captured is held within, so the letters sit inside the run of words
to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A lawyer is told to be careful now that a returning champion has been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Counsel looks like a barrister and 'having captured' like an arrest, but the answer is lying backwards across the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracles is the Greek name of the demigod the Romans called Hercules, the archetypal hero of the twelve labours.

clue.text: Astonished by point made during a rumpus

indicators.note: something that happens during an event sits inside its span, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a compass point
a ruck is a disorderly scrum or brawl

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed by a remark made in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Point is not a remark but one of the four compass directions; it goes after A and before the brawl. A ruck is British slang for a scuffle, and in rugby a loose scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder or amazement, a close synonym of stunned or astonished.

clue.text: Bore being most awfully hurt

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, leaving the letters in a mess

blocks.note: taken as written
ached means hurt, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone tedious complains that they are terribly wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a noun for a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear, meaning put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something unpleasant is to tolerate it, and stomached is an informal past-tense synonym for tolerated.

clue.text: Do settle right inside

indicators.note: a thing placed inside another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An instruction to put things right on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb opening an instruction, but it is the British informal noun for a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a do is a celebration or social event, so it is another word for a gathering of guests.

clue.text: Fine, I’ve boobed pushing back take-off

indicators.note: pushed back means sent the other way, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
the exclamation made on making a mistake

explanation.surface: An airline pilot apologises for delaying the departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing back' and 'take-off' suggest an aircraft leaving the gate, but take-off here is an imitation or parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a humorous imitation mocking someone, which is exactly what a spoof or parody is.

clue.text: Note part of writing shows potential

indicators.note: something that forms part of a whole lies within it

blocks.note: prose is ordinary written language
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A teacher's comment on part of an essay suggests talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows potential' reads as a single verb phrase, but only potential defines; shows links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing promise means displaying signs of future ability, so the noun is a synonym for latent capability.

clue.text: So, these directions may be attached to entrance

definitions.text: these directions may be attached to entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: thus, in such a manner

blocks.clueFragment: these directions may be attached to entrance
blocks.note: second meaning: a sign at a door might read 'In' with an arrow and 'This way'

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic picture: split the answer as IN and THIS WAY and it becomes the kind of sign fixed to an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: So, as an adverb meaning thus or in such a manner, is a direct synonym of the whole phrase.

clue.text: Tool detected after computer system attack

indicators.note: one thing coming after another is placed behind it in the answer

blocks.note: a hack is an unauthorised intrusion into a computer system
saw means noticed or detected

explanation.surface: Malware is spotted after a cyber attack on a network.
explanation.walkthrough: Tool reads as the malicious software of the surface story, but it is a workshop implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw in a frame, used for cutting metal, so it is a hand tool.

clue.text: Engaging professional to take on unknown soldier’s fate

indicators.note: to take something on is to take it aboard, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: able means competent or skilled, as a professional is
missing in action, the status of a soldier whose fate is unknown

explanation.surface: Hiring an expert to investigate what became of a soldier who never came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown soldier' suggests the war memorial, but the phrase defines MIA, the military abbreviation for missing in action.
explanation.definitionFit: An engaging person is pleasant and charming company, which is what amiable, meaning friendly and good-natured, describes.

clue.text: He takes out their tame aunt occasionally

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A dutiful nephew sometimes takes his family's docile aunt out for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes out' reads as escorting someone on an outing, but it is slang for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is underworld slang for killing them, and a hired assassin is the man who does it.

clue.text: Mail son a mysterious iconic image

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and obscure, so these letters are disguised in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Send your boy a puzzling famous picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mysterious' fits the painting's famous enigmatic smile, which makes the anagram signal blend into the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait is probably the most famous and widely reproduced painting in the world, an icon of Western art.

clue.text: Company’s speaking equipment is huge

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, plus the possessive S
a mic, short for microphone, is equipment for speaking into

explanation.surface: A firm's public-address system is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Company's is used to supply the S, a common trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic literally means relating to the universe, and figuratively vast or immense in scale.

clue.text: Son for each male? They get daughters too

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
per means for each, as in per head
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Is there a son for every man? Daughters arrive as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The question invites thinking about families with sons; the definition jokes that these cells, having just been built from son and male, produce daughters as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Male reproductive cells fertilise the egg and determine the child's sex, so they beget girls as well as boys.

clue.text: Manipulating the margins can produce scary scenarios

indicators.note: to manipulate is to handle and rework, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fiddling profit margins could lead to disaster for a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulating the margins' suggests creative accounting, which makes the anagram signal read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightmares are bad dreams and, by extension, any terrifying or disastrous situations.

clue.text: Prison island held Cubans at the centre

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of the word
the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: An island jail where Cuban prisoners were kept, like Guantanamo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held' reads as detained in the prison story, but only its central letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island in 1814, so it served as his place of confinement.

clue.text: Minor accident following get together damaged mount

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: to gel is to come together or bond
a ding is a small dent or collision

explanation.surface: After a social gathering, a fender-bender leaves a vehicle damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged mount' looks like a dented car or bike, but it is a wry definition of a castrated horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelding is a castrated male horse, so a riding animal that has been, in a sense, damaged.

clue.text: Person dieting swaps lobster starter for white fish

indicators.note: to swap is to exchange one thing for another, so a letter is replaced
the starter of a meal comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a slimmer is someone trying to lose weight
its opening letter, which comes out
W is the abbreviation for white

explanation.surface: A dieter replaces a seafood starter with a pale fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobster starter' and 'white fish' read as a menu, but starter is its first letter and fish stands alone as the definition. Slimmer is the British word for a dieter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is a creature that swims, so it can be described by this more general term for anything that swims.
